title: Kernel auto-selection v2 — working notes (scratchpad)
content:
Last updated: 2026-02-24 (Yuki)

Purpose of this doc
- Scratchpad for kernel auto-selection v2: open questions, weird perf results, SKU mapping footguns, and links to ongoing PRs.
- Not the design doc. Expect partial thoughts + TODOs.

Quick context / current state
- v2 selector = rule-based (feature extraction -> candidate set -> ordered preferences -> fallback hierarchy).
- Features we are leaning on right now:
  - model family / architecture tags (Llama/Mistral/Qwen/Gemma-ish)
  - seq-length regime (prefill-heavy vs decode-heavy) + coarse buckets
  - GPU SKU normalization (A100/H100/L40S, with some cloud naming variants)
- Rollout: behind feature gate, allowlist-based, with denylist for known-bad kernel/SKU/driver combos.

Where the issues are showing up (high-level)
1) Long-context prefill misclassification -> tail latency spikes (p99) on some SKUs.
2) GPU SKU naming mismatch -> selector looks up wrong registry row -> falls back to safe-but-slow or (worse) chooses a kernel that’s “supported” but unstable.
3) Mixed workload stability: a route that alternates short chats + occasional long summarization can thrash between kernels unless we anchor on distribution hints.
4) Telemetry overhead: too much cardinality if we emit raw candidate sets / feature values at 100%.

Open questions (still unresolved)
- Seq regime: what do we actually want as the “signal of truth”?
  - Inputs available:
    - request prompt_tokens (known)
    - max_output_tokens (known)
    - observed decode length (only after the fact)
    - scheduler hints (route-level distribution over last N minutes)
  - Question: if scheduler hint says “mostly short”, but we get one long prompt, should we trust request-level bucket or the hint? Current thinking: always trust request-level prefill bucket for safety (avoid long-context spikes), but use hint to break ties within short buckets.

- Model family detection:
  - We currently infer from model config + architecture tag in manifest.
  - Edge cases:
    - fine-tunes with weird naming ("llama-3.1-8b-instruct-foo")
    - GGUF-like variants (not in runtime) but sometimes appear in user docs; ensure we don’t add confusing logic.
  - TODO: decide if “unknown family” should be treated as “conservative” (safe kernel) or “use generic best kernel per SKU”.

- Determinism constraints:
  - Selector must be deterministic for a given (model_version, sku, driver/cuda, seq_bucket, selector_version, config snapshot).
  - Question: do we allow dynamic routing based on “recent perf” in-process? Probably no (nondeterministic + can be unstable). Keep v2 deterministic; anything adaptive should happen in scheduler layer with stable policy engine.

- Fallback hierarchy:
  - Current ordering (rough): (preferred per family+bucket+SKU) -> (alternate per bucket+SKU) -> (generic per SKU) -> (known-stable baseline) -> (runtime default kernel).
  - Open question: how aggressively do we jump to baseline when candidate kernel missing microbench results? We need to avoid silent perf regressions due to incomplete registry rows.
  - Proposal: hard-require “stability bit” per (kernel, sku, driver) and default to baseline if missing.

- Telemetry sampling policy:
  - We need per-request selection traces for debugging, but can’t afford high-cardinality fields at high rate.
  - Current direction: 
    - 100% counters for chosen_kernel (as a low-cardinality tag if we keep the set bounded)
    - sampled “decision event” with candidates/features (1% default; 10% for canary routes; 100% when debug flag enabled)
  - Open: how to prevent exploding tag cardinality when models are numerous? Might need to hash model_id in logs, keep model_family as tag.

Experiments / benchmarks we ran (notes, not final)
(See perf results sheet for actual numbers — these are just the takeaways.)

Exp 1 — long-context summarization (prefill-heavy)
- Workload: prompt 12k–24k tokens, output 512–1k tokens.
- Observation: v2 sometimes chose “fast-decode” kernel because max_output_tokens was high, even though prefill dominated.
- Result: p99 regression on L40S (worse than A100).
- Fix direction: bucket decision should prioritize prompt_tokens; max_output_tokens is secondary.
- Status: addressed in threshold tweak PR (see pr-28522). Need re-run on H100.

Exp 2 — chat (short prompt) + occasional long tool output
- Workload: mostly <1k prompt, output 256, but 5% have 6k tool output (decode heavy).
- Observation: selector switches kernels per request; this is fine, BUT kernel-switch overhead shows up when requests are interleaved on same worker.
- We need to bound “kernel thrash”:
  - maybe pin kernel per worker for small windows?
  - or cluster requests by regime more aggressively in scheduler.
- Action: Sofia + Lena to evaluate passing a regime hint to scheduler for batching (already starting in pr-28502).

Exp 3 — SKU mapping correctness
- Observed mismatches (examples):
  - “NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB” vs “A100 80GB SXM” vs cloud instance label.
  - MIG slices: A100 1g.10gb etc. Do we treat as separate SKU? Probably yes for perf, but registry explosion risk.
- Proposed normalization scheme:
  - sku_family=A100/H100/L40S
  - form_factor=sxm|pcie|unknown
  - mem_gb=40|80|…
  - mig_profile=none|1g10gb|2g20gb|…
- TODO: decide what dimensions are required keys vs optional annotations.
- Safety note: if SKU cannot be normalized to a known key, selector should hard-fallback to baseline (and emit a warning).

Exp 4 — selector overhead
- Microbench shows selector evaluation is cheap in isolation, but telemetry building (candidate lists + features) can be expensive.
- Recommendation: build detailed event only when sampled; always keep “chosen_kernel” + “fallback_level” counters.
- Also consider caching decisions per (model_family, model_variant, sku_key, seq_bucket, selector_version) in-process.
  - BUT ensure cache doesn’t incorporate nondeterministic fields.
  - Also ensure hot reload of allow/deny lists invalidates cache.

Mis-selections / anomalies seen in early testing
(These are the ones we should keep regression tests around.)

Anomaly A — long-context p99 spike on L40S
- Symptom: p99 +18–30% vs v1 on summarization route, only on L40S pool in us-west.
- Hypothesis: mis-bucketed into “mixed/decode” -> picks kernel optimized for decode; prefill suffers.
- Evidence: sampled traces show seq_bucket=mixed when prompt_tokens>16k.
- Fix: adjust bucket boundaries + ensure prompt_tokens dominates. (pr-28522)

Anomaly B — A100 PCIe vs SXM confusion
- Symptom: some A100-PCIe nodes selecting kernel intended for SXM tuning.
- Root cause: sku normalization collapsed both to A100-80 without form factor.
- Mitigation: split key or apply conservative mapping when form factor unknown.
- TODO: confirm perf deltas justify the split; otherwise keep single but ensure chosen kernel is safe across both.

Anomaly C — “unknown model family” falling into aggressive default
- Symptom: a few internal eval models (custom variants) were tagged unknown and got generic best-per-SKU kernel; one variant hit a correctness bug (numerical mismatch) on older driver.
- Action: for unknown family: restrict to “known-stable baseline” kernel unless explicitly allowlisted.
- Also: guardrail disable v2 on driver combos where we haven’t validated. (pr-28495)

Anomaly D — denylist hot reload not taking effect quickly enough
- Symptom: oncall toggled denylist, but workers continued choosing bad kernel for ~2–3 minutes.
- Suspect: config refresh interval + cached decisions.
- Requirement: denylist updates must invalidate cache immediately (or keep cache TTL very low during canary).
- TODO: coordinate with Jordan/Benji on policy engine + hot reload semantics.

Notes from threads / decisions (quick captures)
- Rule-based vs learned scoring: consensus is rule-based for v2 (explainability, safer rollback). Keep door open for learned scoring offline to propose registry updates, but not in the hot path.
- Determinism: selector should not depend on runtime counters or wall-clock randomness. If we sample telemetry, sampling decision must not change the selected kernel.

TODO list (near term)
- [Yuki] Add regression test cases for seq bucket boundaries (esp 8k/16k/32k prompt lengths).
- [Isabella] Validate kernel-switch overhead numbers with realistic concurrency (not just microbench); quantify benefit of caching.
- [Grace] Confirm known-stable baseline kernel list per SKU + driver; update denylist seed file.
- [Omar] Finalize telemetry fields + sampling defaults for canary; ensure no PII and cap cardinality.
- [Sofia/Lena] Make sure scheduler hint integration can’t override request-level safety for long-context.
- [Benji/Jordan] Clarify hot reload + cache invalidation semantics (denylist must be fast).

Release/canary notes to remember
- Canary should start with:
  - a narrow model allowlist (top 2–3 model families) + single region + known-good SKU
  - higher telemetry sampling (but watch ingestion costs)
  - explicit rollback trigger: p99 regression > X% for long-context bucket, or error rate threshold, or kernel crash signal
- Ensure oncall runbook includes:
  - disable v2 by model+region
  - pin kernel (force) as workaround
  - how to pull a “selection trace” for a specific request_id

Links / pointers (for me)
- Core selector logic: pr-28411
- Model family classifier: pr-28428
- Seq bucket & prefill/decode heuristics: pr-28439
- SKU-aware registry + fallback: pr-28452
- Feature gate plumbing: pr-28460
- Telemetry events: pr-28466
- Deterministic replay tests: pr-28473
- Debug CLI flags (force kernel, dump selection): pr-28481
- Driver guardrail: pr-28495
- Scheduler hint integration: pr-28502
- Allow/deny list rules + hot reload: pr-28510
- Long-context regression fix: pr-28522

Appendix — “definition of done” reminders (non-negotiables)
- Zero correctness regressions (numerical / output mismatch beyond tolerated precision).
- Deterministic selection for identical inputs + config snapshot.
- No unbounded tag cardinality (telemetry).
- Fast rollback (feature gate + denylist) with predictable blast radius.
